body:
A vault of typed markdown, a CLI the agent operates, a methodology bundle and a human view; the harness runs every agent

## TL;DR

Anvil is four parts around one loop: a vault of typed markdown, a CLI the agent operates, a methodology bundle of skills and agents, and a human view. The harness runs every agent. The human works at the milestone; anvil works at the issue. Each gate on the path is code that reads vault evidence.

## Context and scope

The **vault** is a directory of typed, linked markdown artifacts for all projects. It is the only source of truth. The **CLI** is the one way to change the vault. The agent operates it. The **methodology bundle** is the skills, agents and session guide that tell the agent when to call the CLI and what to do with the result. The **human view** is a local UI from the same binary. In it the human reads the vault.

The agent harness sits outside anvil. It starts every agent, session and subagent. Anvil's skills tell the main agent which subagents to dispatch.

Work runs in two loops. In the outer loop, the human chooses a milestone, approves it and accepts its result. In the inner loop, anvil implements each issue of that milestone, brings its PR to green and lands it on the human's approval. Each step writes artifacts through the CLI. Each later step reads them back. The loop's state lives in the vault, not in the agent's session.

*Diagram [`anvil-two-loop`](/projects/bp/designs/system/diagrams/anvil-two-loop.html) renders on this page's canvas in anvil ui.*

Anvil talks to these systems and stops at their edge.

*Diagram [`anvil-context`](/projects/bp/designs/system/diagrams/anvil-context.html) renders on this page's canvas in anvil ui.*

- **Claude Code.** It loads the bundle. Hooks call the binary at session start, before compaction and at session end. A harness permission rule can gate the land command.
- **Codex.** It receives translated copies of skills and agents, and no hooks.
- **An agent orchestrator, such as Paseo.** It runs agents, owns workspaces and holds the schedules. Anvil treats it as one provider of a workspace and a dispatch command. The binary never names it. `--cut-worktree` plus harness subagents stay the built-in provider.
- **Vault directory.** Plain files. Any markdown editor can read them. No editor is a dependency.
- **git.** Anvil creates one worktree for each issue and removes it after the land.
- **gh CLI.** Anvil reads PR state and runs the merge after the human's approval.
- **Browser.** The human view runs on the local machine only: stdlib `net/http` + `html/template` + `goldmark` (raw HTML off), decided 2026-10-08.
- **GitHub vault backup.** A session-end hook commits and pushes the vault.

## Non-goals

- No orchestrator of anvil's own. The harness dispatches, supervises and schedules agents.
- No merge queue. One human approves one PR at a time.
- No database beyond the disposable index. Files plus agent search serve one user's vault.
- No dashboard for agent sessions. The human view shows the vault only.
- No transcript archive. A distilled learning carries more than a raw transcript.
- No shared vault or permissions. Team features wait until a team asks.
- No full spec-to-code sync. Anvil stops at code-reference stamps and stale flags.

## Constraints and quality goals

- **One static Go binary.** cobra with fang for the CLI. `git` and `gh` are subprocesses, never libraries.
- **Storage is markdown with YAML frontmatter**, in a git-versioned vault outside any source repo. One JSON Schema per artifact type, embedded in the binary.
- **The index is SQLite** through the pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite` driver. It is a cache derived from the vault. Deleting it loses nothing.
- **Distribution.** The user installs the binary. The binary supplies the bundle and installs it into each harness.
- **No new top-level dependency without the human's approval.** [[shared/conventions/convention.cli-tooling]] governs each verb: non-interactive, `--json` on reads, idempotent mutations.
- **Context is scarce.** Every skill, field and doc must earn its tokens. The agent loads the artifacts that govern one task, at the start of that task.
- **The harness changes monthly.** Anvil wraps native features thinly and does not rebuild them.
- **The project's default branch is protected.** No direct push, no force-push, CI must pass, and the branch must be up to date before a merge.
- **Local only.** No network call beyond `git`, `gh` and the harness. The human view binds to localhost.
- **Readable cold.** Every artifact follows [[shared/conventions/convention.prose]], so the human and the agent can both check it. The vault stays readable if anvil disappears.
- **Tests:** stdlib `testing` with `go-cmp`; an integration build tag for tests that drive the built binary. [[shared/conventions/convention.testing]] sets the bar.

## Components

Components are cut by responsibility, not by Go package. A component design is written when a milestone first needs an interface others build against.

| Component | Responsibility | Component design |
|---|---|---|
| **Artifact model** | The vault files and their rules: types (a per-project data model among them), ids, links, state tables, validation at write | [[projects/bp/designs/components/artifact-model]] |
| **Index** | A derived store for queries: lists, the ready queue, the link graph, search | — |
| **Verb surface** | The verbs, flags, output and error formats that the agent calls | — |
| **Context assembly** | What the agent sees and when: session guide, `hydrate`, learnings retrieval, handoff and resume | — |
| **Lifecycle** | A milestone's path from shaped to accepted, each issue's path from ready to resolved, their gates and their evidence | [[projects/bp/designs/components/lifecycle]] |
| **Integrity checks** | Checks after the write and over time: `validate`, `doctor`, drift, inbox age | [[projects/bp/designs/components/integrity-checks]] |
| **Methodology bundle** | Skills, pinned-model agents and the session guide | — |
| **Installer** | Delivery of the bundle and its hooks into each harness | — |
| **Human view** | How the human reads the vault: a local, read-only UI that replaces Obsidian | [[projects/bp/designs/components/human-view]] |

Nine, not eight: milestones cite this set in their Components changed line, so it stays stable.

## Runtime flow

The critical path is one milestone. The milestone carries the end goal, the finish line and the design change. The design docs describe the accepted state. The milestone holds what it changes in them, and anvil applies the change at acceptance. An abandoned milestone leaves the design docs untouched.

Anvil derives the issues a few at a time, against the current code. The human approves the milestone, not a list of issues. The worker finds the how, within the constraints that the vault gives it.

Each loop has exits beyond success. The inner loop stops when the milestone proves wrong or an issue reaches its round limit. The outer loop stops at the milestone's size limit. Every stop returns to the human at the milestone gate: amend, cut scope or abandon.

Each step is marked `(shipped)` or `(target)`.

*Diagram [`anvil-runtime-flow`](/projects/bp/designs/system/diagrams/anvil-runtime-flow.html) renders on this page's canvas in anvil ui.*

**Where the finish line runs.** `milestone status` and `transition milestone done` run the predicates in the project's main checkout, not in a worktree. The checkout must sit at the tip of the default branch, as `origin/HEAD` names it. The verb refuses when the checkout is off that tip; without a remote it warns and measures the current checkout. The caller runs `git pull --ff-only` first.

The human acts at four points: the choice, the milestone, each green PR and the result. The milestone matters most, because it comes before any code. Three checks support the human: the milestone gate before approval, the create gate before an issue enters the queue, and the finish line before acceptance.

Outside the loop, two rules keep the vault true over time. Every key decision starts with a thread, and the decision cites it. Integrity checks flag a design doc, convention or inbox item that is stale, drifted or unreadable. A flag opens a thread; the thread settles into a decision; the decision revises the doc. Shaping a milestone reads every inbox item routed to it.

## System invariants

Cross-component rules. Planning checks against them; review verifies them.

1. The vault is the only source of truth. The index can be deleted at any time.
2. The CLI's write path is the only way into the vault. The human view has no write path.
3. The anvil binary never starts an agent process. The harness starts all agents, and anvil's skills tell it which ones.
4. A skill names only verbs, skills and paths that exist.
5. Anvil brings each PR to green without the human. The human sees a PR only when its verification, its review and its CI all pass at the current commit.
6. The design docs describe the accepted state. A milestone changes them only at acceptance.

Rules a component design owns, linked and never copied here:

- A worker cannot change the verification that judges it: [[projects/bp/designs/components/lifecycle]], the verification lock.
- A PR merges only on the human's approval at its head, and evidence names its commit: [[projects/bp/designs/components/lifecycle]], the land gate.
- No issue is claimed before its milestone is approved: [[projects/bp/designs/components/lifecycle]], the milestone gate.
- A milestone is done only when its issues are closed and the human accepted the result: [[projects/bp/designs/components/lifecycle]], the acceptance gate.
- A write validates first and lands whole: [[projects/bp/designs/components/artifact-model]], validate at write.
- A decision names the thread that produced it: [[projects/bp/designs/components/artifact-model]], the decision-thread link.
- A check never reports success on input it did not examine: [[projects/bp/designs/components/integrity-checks]], examine before pass.

## Decisions

- [[projects/bp/decisions/vault-backup-discipline.0001-vault-backup-discipline-handoff-nudge-plus-user]] — the vault backup boundary; its no-push ruling is superseded by the session-end hook.
- [[projects/bp/decisions/anvil-build-revival.0002-remove-anvil-build]] — `anvil build` is removed; the harness runs all agents.
- [[projects/bp/decisions/merge-approval.0001-the-human-approves-each-pr-at-its-head-the-agent-runs-the-me]] — the human approves at the PR head; the agent merges behind a permission prompt.
- [[projects/bp/decisions/merge-approval.0002-approval-is-per-pr-not-per-milestone]] — approval is per PR.
- [[projects/bp/decisions/design-type-model.0002-the-design-change-lives-in-the-milestone-until-acceptance]] — the design change lives in the milestone until acceptance.
- [[projects/bp/decisions/design-layout.0003-anvil-ships-its-own-human-view-in-place-of-obsidian]] — anvil ships its own human view.

## Open questions

- How the bundle reaches Claude Code: the harness installs a bundle the binary supplies, or the binary copies it. Owner: the Installer component design, when its milestone starts.
- What the claim must record when a harness-owned workspace replaces anvil's worktree. Open in [[shared/threads/anvil-design-docs.0003-what-does-paseo-replace-in-anvil-and-what-must-the-claim]].
- How the land gate proves the human's approval in a session that skips permission prompts. Owner: the candidate milestone "Protect the merge" in [[projects/bp/designs/product]].

## Solution strategy

- The vault is plain files in git, so the project stays explainable if anvil disappears. The index holds no fact the vault lacks.
- The CLI is the only door, so one place validates each write and one place assembles context for one task.
- The harness runs the agents. Anvil keeps what the harness lacks: a design spine, a verification on each issue, context for one issue, one vault across projects. [[projects/bp/decisions/anvil-build-revival.0002-remove-anvil-build]]
- The human works at the milestone, in the author's words: "I think about the component/milestone to be implemented and then the anvil system creates the context to then implement." The issue is anvil's unit.
- Gates are code that reads vault evidence, because prose gates were skipped: a worker opened a PR on a red verification, and a worker rewrote its own predicate.
- The human approves and the agent merges: "Once I've reviewed the PR I often tell the agent to merge for me." [[projects/bp/decisions/merge-approval.0001-the-human-approves-each-pr-at-its-head-the-agent-runs-the-me]]
- Anvil has its own UI, because the human must read what the agent reads. [[projects/bp/decisions/design-layout.0003-anvil-ships-its-own-human-view-in-place-of-obsidian]]
